info.title: FerrisCD Control Plane API
info.description: In-process REST API of the FerrisCD GitOps control plane (ADR-002). `GET .../diff` and `GET .../resources` are computed live from the same `RepoCache`, renderer cache, `ClusterManager` and SSA dry-run diff the controller reconciles with, so an API answer can never disagree with the next reconcile. All diff payloads are `Secret`-redacted before they leave the engine.

get.summary: Lists every `Application` this control plane watches, filtered to the caller's projects.
get.description: Every `Application` this control plane watches, with its sync/health verdict. Filtered to the projects the caller is authorized for: anything outside them is absent, exactly as if it did not exist.

200.description: Every watched Application the caller may see

502.description: The cluster could not be read

get.summary: The SSE dashboard feed (`T17.3`): `text/event-stream` of RBAC-filtered `Application` snapshots.
get.description: A `text/event-stream` feed of `Application` snapshots, each filtered to the projects the caller is authorized for (a snapshot never contains another tenant's application). Authenticated with the standard `Authorization: Bearer` header — never a query parameter, which is why the UI consumes it with `fetch()` streaming. A snapshot failure ends the stream with one `error` frame so the client can fall back to polling.

200.description: A `text/event-stream` of RBAC-filtered `Application` snapshots (`event: applications`, one `ApplicationListView` JSON body per frame)

get.description: One `Application`, with its conditions, deployment history, and running operation. An application in a project the caller may not see answers exactly the 404 a nonexistent one answers.

403.description: The caller may see this Application but not read it

404.description: No such Application, or none visible to the caller

502.description: The cluster could not be read

get.summary: Computes the live, Secret-redacted diff of an `Application` (`T14.1`).
get.description: The live, `Secret`-redacted Server-Side-Apply dry-run diff. Computed by the controller's own pipeline in-process, and read-only: nothing is applied, pruned, or patched.

403.description: The caller may see this Application but not diff it

404.description: No such Application, or none visible to the caller

502.description: The diff could not be computed

get.summary: Reads the Kubernetes `Event`s that regard an `Application` (`T17.3`).
get.description: The latest Kubernetes `events.k8s.io/v1` events about one `Application` (`Normal`/`Warning`), newest first and bounded to 50. Read strictly from the `Application`'s own namespace with a `regarding.uid` field selector (never cluster-wide), and every note is `Secret`/token redacted.

403.description: The caller may see this Application but not read it

404.description: No such Application, or none visible to the caller

502.description: The cluster could not be read

get.summary: Reads the live resource graph of an `Application` (`T14.1`).
get.description: The live resource graph: `status.inventory` read on demand from the destination cluster, plus `Deployment -> ReplicaSet -> Pod` children discovered through `metadata.ownerReferences` (no informers). One listing per (cluster, namespace, kind) per request, bounded by `MAX_GRAPH_NODES` and `MAX_GRAPH_LIST_REQUESTS`.

403.description: The caller may see this Application but not read it

404.description: No such Application, or none visible to the caller

502.description: The destination cluster could not be read

post.summary: Requests a rollback to a history entry (`T14.1`).
post.description: Requests a rollback by patching `ferriscd.io/operation` to `{"rollback":{"id":N}}`. The id must exist in `status.history`. A rollback supersedes a pending manual sync or an earlier rollback (one annotation slot) and is consumed by the controller once applied.

400.description: The body is not the expected JSON

403.description: The caller may see this Application but not roll it back

404.description: No such Application, or none visible to the caller

409.description: The Application changed while the request was recorded

422.description: No history entry with that id

post.description: Requests a reconcile by patching `ferriscd.io/operation` to `{"sync":{}}`. The controller does the work; this endpoint never syncs anything itself, and the controller consumes the annotation once a pass has settled. A pending manual sync answers 202 (idempotent); only a pending rollback is a conflict.

dryRun.description: Compute the sync without applying it. **Not supported in `v1.0`**: that is `GET .../diff`.

prune.description:
Prune orphans after the sync. **Not supported in `v1.0`**: pruning is a spec field
(`syncPolicy.automated.prune`).

revision.description: Pin the sync to a specific revision. **Not supported in `v1.0`** (see [`sync_application`]).

202.description: The sync request was recorded (or is already pending)

403.description: The caller may see this Application but not sync it

404.description: No such Application, or none visible to the caller

409.description: A rollback is pending, or the Application changed

get.description:
Validates that `state` is **this browser's** (the [`STATE_COOKIE_NAME`] cookie must equal the query
parameter, compared in constant time), consumes the one-shot transaction, exchanges the code with
the stored verifier, seals a session cookie plus the CSRF cookie, and answers `303` to the
configured post-login path. The state cookie is expired on the response whatever the outcome.

303.description: Session established; redirect to the post-login path

400.description: The state is missing, unknown, expired or not this browser's

401.description: The session cookie could not be sealed

404.description: The BFF flow is not enabled on this server

502.description: The identity provider could not be reached

get.summary:
Publishes how a caller can authenticate, so the Web UI and the CLI can pick a sign-in flow
(`T19.1`; `T19.2` consumes it with PKCE).
get.description: How to authenticate against this server: the auth mode (token-review, oidc, token-review-or-oidc, ...), plus the OIDC issuer, public client id and scopes when OIDC is enabled. Public by design — a client needs it before it has a credential.

Answers `302` to the IdP's authorization endpoint with a fresh `state`, `nonce` and `S256`
challenge — plus the short-lived [`STATE_COOKIE_NAME`] cookie that binds that `state` to this
browser — or `404` when the server was started without `--oidc-bff-enabled`.

`429` is the per-client sign-in budget ([`MAX_LOGINS_PER_CLIENT`] per [`LOGIN_WINDOW`]).

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: The registered redirect URI; must match exactly

302.description: Redirect to the identity provider's authorization endpoint

400.description: redirect_uri is not the registered one

404.description: The BFF flow is not enabled on this server

429.description: Too many sign-ins were started from this address

502.description: The identity provider's discovery document is unavailable

post.description:
Requires the double-submit CSRF header (see [`csrf`]) for a *usable* session: a cross-site page
must not be able to sign an operator out. A request the browser labels cross-site is refused
outright, even with no session cookie at all — otherwise any page could force the `Max-Age=0`
cookies to be stored. A cookie that no longer opens (expired, tampered, sealed under a rotated
key) is treated as absent here, because the caller's only remaining goal is to get rid of it —
refusing that would leave the browser stuck behind a `401` it cannot clear.

The session is stateless, so this cannot revoke a cookie that was copied before the sign-out: that
copy keeps working until the token (or the cookie) expires; only the IdP can revoke it earlier.

403.description: The CSRF header is missing or does not match, or the sign-out was initiated from another site

404.description: The BFF flow is not enabled on this server

get.summary: Lists addressable clusters visible to the caller's authorized `AppProject`s (`T13.1`, `T17.1`).
get.description: The cluster registry filtered to clusters permitted by the caller's visible `AppProject`s: `in-cluster` first, then matching registered cluster names.

502.description: The cluster could not be read

get.description: This OpenAPI 3.1 document. The same bytes are committed to `docs/api/openapi.json` and used to generate the TypeScript client.

502.description: The document could not be serialized

get.summary: Lists every `AppProject` of the control-plane namespace the caller may see.
get.description: Every `AppProject` of the control-plane namespace, with its repository, namespace, destination, and ServiceAccount allow-lists.

502.description: The cluster could not be read

post.description: GitHub push webhook. Authenticated by `X-Hub-Signature-256` (HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body, constant-time) and replay-protected by `X-GitHub-Delivery`. Responds 202 with how many Applications matched; nothing is applied here.

200.description: The push was accepted and a refresh scheduled, or a replayed delivery / non-push event was ignored (`status` says which)

401.description: The signature is missing or wrong

post.description: GitLab push webhook. Authenticated by the `X-Gitlab-Token` shared secret (constant-time); GitLab signs nothing, so the token is the whole authentication. Responds 202 with how many Applications matched; nothing is applied here.

200.description: The push was accepted and a refresh scheduled, or a non-push event was ignored (`status` says which)

401.description: The token is missing or wrong

get.summary: Liveness probe: the process is running and the router answers.

Readiness probe: `503` until the control plane's startup gates (`Application` watches,
`ClusterManager` initial `Secret` seed, and initial `ferriscd-rbac-cm` load) have all completed
`InitDone` (`T17.1`).

ApiErrorBody.description:
The body of a failed request.

`Deserialize` as well as `Serialize` because it is the contract in **both** directions: the
`ferriscd` CLI (`T14.5`) maps a refused request back onto this shape instead of re-inventing one.

ApiErrorDetail.description: One failure, in the shape the OpenAPI document declares.

oneOf.description: The running operation, when one is recorded.

items.description: The latest events, newest first, at most 50.

truncated.description: Whether the cluster holds more events about this `Application` than the `items` list carries.

ApplicationEventView.description: One Kubernetes `Event` about an `Application`, as the timeline renders it.

count.description: How many times the event recurred.

firstObservedAt.description: When it was first observed (RFC 3339 UTC), when the cluster recorded it.

lastObservedAt.description: When it was last observed (RFC 3339 UTC), when the cluster recorded it.

message.description: `note`, redacted: no URL credential, `Secret` payload, or token survives here.

ApplicationSummary.description: One `Application`, reduced to what a UI/CLI lists.

conditions.description: `status.conditions`, newest last, exactly as the controller wrote them.

AuthConfigView.description:
`GET /api/v1/auth/config` body (`T19.1`).

Served from the **public** group: the SPA and `ferriscd login --oidc` must learn how to
authenticate before they have a token, so this carries only what a stranger may know — the auth
mode, the issuer, the public client id and the scopes (`T19.2` consumes it).

bffEnabled.description: Whether the optional server-side (BFF cookie) session mode is enabled (`T19.2`).

clientId.description: The configured OAuth client id. **Absent** when OIDC is disabled; never `null`.

issuer.description: The configured OIDC issuer. **Absent** when OIDC is disabled; never `null`.

scopes.description: The scopes the client should request from the IdP. Always present (`[]` when OIDC is off).

items.description: `in-cluster` first, then every registered cluster name.

inCluster.description: Whether this is the cluster the control plane runs in.

observedGeneration.description: `metadata.generation` observed when the condition was computed.

DiffChangeView.description: One field-level change of a diffed resource.

path.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the redacted object.

field.description: The disputed field, as reported by the API server.

manager.description: The manager that owns the field.

truncated.description: Whether the change list was cut by the engine's bound.

missing.description: Resources that do not exist yet.

orphaned.description: Tracked resources no longer in Git.

synced.description: Resources whose live state matches the prediction.

desired.description: How many resources the rendered bundle contains.

resources.description: One entry per resource in `desired ∪ status.inventory`.

revision.description: Commit the desired state was rendered from.

wouldSync.description: Whether the sync decision gate would apply this set right now.

request.description: The exact `ferriscd.io/operation` value that was patched.

resourceVersion.description: The resource version the patch was conditioned on, when it was read.

finishedAt.description: When it finished (RFC 3339), absent while running.

revision.description: Revision the operation is working on.

ProjectView.description: One `AppProject`, reduced to its boundary facts.

cluster.description: Cluster the graph was read from (`spec.destination.cluster`).

namespace.description: Namespace the graph was read from (`spec.destination.namespace`).

nodes.description: Inventory nodes plus discovered `Deployment -> ReplicaSet -> Pod` children.

truncated.description: Whether the response was cut at [`MAX_GRAPH_NODES`].

ResourceNodeView.description: One node of the resource graph.

group.description: API group (empty for the core group).

health.description: Per-resource health from the last reconcile (`status.resourceStatuses`).

healthMessage.description: The health message of the last reconcile.

ownership.description: Ownership verdict for a present object.

parent.description: GKNN of the owning node (`Deployment -> ReplicaSet -> Pod`), absent for roots.

present.description: Whether the object exists in the destination cluster right now.

repoUrl.description: Repository URL, redacted (a remote URL may carry a token).

dryRun.description: Compute the sync without applying it. **Not supported in `v1.0`**: that is `GET .../diff`.

prune.description:
Prune orphans after the sync. **Not supported in `v1.0`**: pruning is a spec field
(`syncPolicy.automated.prune`).

revision.description: Pin the sync to a specific revision. **Not supported in `v1.0`** (see [`sync_application`]).

WebhookResponse.description: The `ferriscd.io/refresh` request a webhook reports back.

message.description: Why nothing was done (`ignored`), or which delivery id was a replay.

repository.description: The pushed repository, redacted (a remote URL may carry a token).
